prov.heading: Provision for Credit Losses
prov.text:
Three Months Ended September 30, 2026 Compared to Three Months Ended June 30, 2026

The Company recorded a provision for credit losses of $3.2 million for the third quarter of 2026, compared with $714 thousand in the prior quarter. The provision for credit losses in the third quarter of 2026 was comprised of a $3.2 million provision for credit losses on loans held for investment, partially offset by a $16 thousand reversal of provision for credit losses for unfunded loan commitments. Total unfunded loan commitments decreased by $34.5 million to $862.4 million at September 30, 2026, compared to $896.9 million in unfunded loan commitments at June 30, 2026.

The provision for credit losses for loans held for investment in the third quarter of 2026 was $3.2 million, an increase of $2.2 million from $1.1 million in the prior quarter. The increase reflected $4.6 million in net charge-offs, primarily related to the full charge-off of two commercial and industrial loans, updates to the reasonable and supportable economic forecasts for California, revised scenario weighting assumptions, continued loan growth, and changes in portfolio composition, partially offset by a decline in accruing substandard and special mention loan balances and refinements to the qualitative factors.

nonint.heading: Noninterest Expense
nonint.text:
The following table sets forth the various components of our noninterest expense for the periods indicated:

Three Months Ended September 30, 2026 Compared to Three Months Ended June 30, 2026

Total noninterest expense for the third quarter of 2026 was $24.4 million, an increase of $57 thousand, compared with $24.3 million in the prior quarter. Salaries and employee benefits decreased $157 thousand during the third quarter of 2026 to $15.4 million primarily due to lower overall payroll tax and incentive accruals, partially offset by a decrease in loan origination costs deferred based on decreased loan origination activity. Legal, audit and professional expense increased $229 thousand during the third quarter of 2026. Other real estate owned expenses decreased $197 thousand in the third quarter of 2026 primarily from overall lower holding costs.

Efficiency ratio for the third quarter of 2026 was 53.0%, compared with 54.2% in the prior quarter.

Three Months Ended September 30, 2026 Compared to Three Months Ended September 30, 2025

Total noninterest expense during the three months ended September 30, 2026 was $24.4 million, an increase of $1.0 million compared with total noninterest expense of $23.4 million for the same 2025 period.

tax.heading: Income Taxes
tax.text:
Three Months Ended September 30, 2026 Compared to Three Months Ended June 30, 2026

In the third quarter of 2026, the Company’s income tax expense was $4.4 million, compared with $5.5 million for the second quarter of 2026. The effective rate was 23.9% for the third quarter of 2026 and 27.9% for the second quarter of 2026. The decrease in income tax expense and the effective tax rate for the third quarter of 2026 was primarily driven by a $725 thousand tax benefit recognized from tax credits purchased in the third quarter of 2026.

Three Months Ended September 30, 2026 Compared to Three Months Ended September 30, 2025

Income tax expense for the three months ended September 30, 2026 was $4.4 million, compared to $6.1 million for the same 2025 period. The effective rate was 23.9% during the three months ended September 30, 2026, compared to 28.1% for the same 2025 period. The decrease in the effective tax rate between periods was primarily attributable to the $725 thousand tax benefit recognized from tax credits purchased in the third quarter of 2026.

Nine Months Ended September 30, 2026 Compared to Nine Months Ended September 30, 2025

Income tax expense for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 was $15.3 million, compared to income tax expense of $18.9 million for the same 2025 period.

net.heading: Net Income
net.text:
Three Months Ended September 30, 2026 Compared to Three Months Ended June 30, 2026

Net income for the third quarter of 2026 was $14.0 million, or $0.43 per diluted share, compared with $14.3 million, or $0.44 per diluted share in the second quarter of 2026. Pre-tax, pre-provision income for the third quarter was $21.6 million, an increase of $1.1 million from the prior quarter. The $284 thousand decrease in net income and $0.01 decrease in diluted earnings per share were largely driven by a $2.5 million increase in provision for credit losses and higher noninterest expense of $57 thousand, partially offset by a $790 thousand increase in net interest income and a $351 thousand increase in noninterest income, and a $1.1 million decrease in income taxes.

Three Months Ended September 30, 2026 Compared to Three Months Ended September 30, 2025

Net income for the three months ended September 30, 2026 was $14.0 million, or $0.43 per diluted share, compared with $15.7 million, or $0.48 per diluted share for the same 2025 period. Pre-tax, pre-provision income for the third quarter of 2026 was $21.6 million, a decrease of $158 thousand from the same 2025 period.

ocf.text: Operating activities provided $31.4 million and $36.4 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 and 2025. The primary sources of funds were net income from operations and adjustments to net income, such as other intangible amortization resulting from the prior merger, deferred income taxes, stock-based compensation, the accretion of net discount and deferred loan fees, and provision for (reversal of) credit losses.

Net interest income.heading: Net Interest Income and Margin
Net interest income.text: Net interest income is our primary source of revenue, which is the difference between interest income on loans, debt securities and other investments (collectively, “interest-earning assets”) and interest expense on deposits and borrowings (collectively, “interest-bearing liabilities”). Net interest margin represents net interest income expressed as a percentage of interest-earning assets. Net interest income is affected by changes in volume, mix, and rates of interest-earning assets and interest-bearing liabilities, as well as days in a period. We closely monitor both total net interest income and the net interest margin and seek to maximize net interest income without exposing us to an excessive level of interest rate risk through our asset and liability management policies. Other charges and fees increased $260 thousand in the third quarter of 2026 due primarily to a $30 thousand loss from equity investments in the third quarter of 2026, compared to a loss from equity investments of $251 thousand in the prior quarter.

Three Months Ended September 30, 2026 Compared to Three Months Ended September 30, 2025

Total noninterest income was $1.9 million in the third quarter of 2026, a decrease of $766 thousand compared with $2.7 million in the third quarter of 2025. Bank owned life insurance income decreased $382 thousand primarily related to a death benefit recognized in the third quarter of 2025. No comparable death benefit income was recognized in the third quarter of 2026.

intro.text: California BanCorp is a California corporation incorporated on October 2, 2019 and is registered with the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System as a bank holding company for California Bank of Commerce, N.A. under the Bank Holding Company Act of 1956, as amended. On May 15, 2020, the Company completed a reorganization whereby the Bank became a wholly-owned subsidiary of the Company. California Bank of Commerce, N.A. began business operations in December 2001 under the name Ramona National Bank. The Bank changed its name to First Business Bank, N.A. in 2006, to Bank of Southern California, N.A. in 2010, and to California Bank of Commerce, N.A. on July 31, 2024. The Bank has a wholly-owned subsidiary, BCAL OREO1, LLC, which was incorporated on February 14, 2024. BCAL OREO1, LLC is used for holding other real estate owned and other assets acquired by foreclosure.

A director of the Company is a member of the Investment Committee for Launchpad.

lines.why: Acquired technology, brands and customer relationships: operating.

accounts.note: Acquisitions add goodwill and intangibles at their allocated values, not at the cash paid; the residual is the difference and the amortisation.

accounts.name: Equity
accounts.note: Other comprehensive income (currency translation, unrealised gains) moves equity without passing through net income: it is in the residual.

accounts.name: Cash and equivalents
accounts.note: The cash flow statement's cash can include restricted cash the balance sheet shows elsewhere: a small residual is that difference.

accounts.name: Investments
accounts.note: Securities bought and sold sit in 'other investing' with everything else the section does not name.
